title: Tenant Shield: proactive tenant separation and quota enforcement for Dedicated GPUs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Implement a Tenant Shield capability for Dedicated GPU pools that enforces per-tenant throughput budgets, provides soft and hard quotas, and proactively mitigates noisy neighbor effects while preserving latency SLOs. Scope covers API surface for quota contracts, runtime admission controls, eviction/mitigation heuristics, and telemetry for billing/alerts.

Design overview: introduce a lightweight tenant controller that binds a tenant to an isolation profile (affinity-group, burst-escrow, shaping window). The controller exposes two contract modes: guaranteed-throughput (hard tokens per minute) and best-effort-with-guardrail (soft window + graceful degradation). At the serving runtime we add an admission gate that checks a per-tenant token bucket and a scoring function that ranks inflight requests for preemption when pressure is detected.

Mitigation strategies (progressive): 1) Adaptive shaping: slow token issuance per tenant based on recent latency miss rate. 2) Prefix/KV cache quotas: limit cache memory and hit-penalties per tenant to avoid disproportionate cache thrashing. 3) Proactive lane rebalance: when one tenant's burst would violate neighbors' SLOs, attempt transient lane reassignment to spare capacity pools (fallback to preemption if no spare). 4) Graceful degradation: reduce batch sizes or switch to quantized model variant for excess traffic with telemetry annotated to the trace.

Autoscaling interplay: quota controller integrates with reserved-pool autoscaler through a rate projection RPC. Tenants with guaranteed contracts can trigger scale actions; best-effort tenants cannot cause scale beyond a configured burst ceiling. We will expose autoscale hints in the console and add safeguards to prevent oscillation (cooldown windows and debounce).

Telemetry & observability: per-tenant metrics: allocated_tokens, used_tokens, token_loss, preemptions, avg_latency_p50/p95, cache_evictions. Alerts for when a tenant crosses 90% of guaranteed throughput or causes >5% of cluster p95 regression. Billing export will consume used_tokens for cost reconciliation.

Trade-offs considered: hard quotas protect neighbors but may increase tail latency for the throttled tenant. Soft quotas preserve throughput but complicate billing and SLA reasoning. We aim for a hybrid default: soft with auto-escalation to hard under repeated violations and explicit customer contract.

Migration: existing Dedicated tenants default to "soft-with-guardrail". Customers can opt into guaranteed-throughput via Console or API. Migration plan includes a two-week pilot with opt-in and a retention period before hard enforcement.

Docs & artifacts: design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Tenant+Shield+Design, initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4128, console spec: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2bTenantShieldSpec, demo dashboard prototype: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/tenant-shield-prototype.

Next steps: land runtime admission gate prototype behind feature flag, add token issuer and basic metrics, run chaos tests to validate fair-share under synthetic noisy tenants, then implement console controls and billing export.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a tenant admission gate and token-bucket enforcement behind feature flag
Per-tenant metrics (allocated_tokens, used_tokens, preemptions, p95_latency) emitted to telemetry backend
Autoscaler honors guaranteed-throughput contracts and respects burst ceilings for best-effort tenants
Console shows tenant contract, current usage, and allows switching between soft/hard modes
Pilot run with 3 customers demonstrating <1% cluster p95 regression when protected tenants are active
Billing export maps used_tokens to billing rows for dedicated capacity contracts
notes: We will coordinate with Sales for customers interested in guaranteed-throughput before enabling hard enforcement. Security to review token-issuer RPC and telemetry access controls. Performance team will run end-to-end benchmarks on GPU families used by Dedicated (A100/V100 equivalents).
